parsed.n_justification: The Upper Iowa River basin (NE Iowa / SE Minnesota) agricultural landscape spans a texture gradient from sandy loams on outwash and alluvial terraces to silty clay loams on till-derived uplands (Mollisols). Five columns hold climate forcing and vegetation constant while spanning the dominant USDA texture classes, isolating texture as the single controlling variable and giving enough contrast to quantify its strength on sub-surface drainage.
assumptions: Climate forcing, vegetation (managed C3/corn-soy or generic crop PFT), slope, and aspect are held identical across all columns so soil texture is the only varying control
A multi-year (>=200 yr accelerated + final) spinup precedes the 20-year evaluation run to equilibrate soil moisture and water table
Sub-surface drainage is diagnosed from ELM's QDRAI (baseflow/drainage) and QDRAI_PERCH terms; single-column ELM lacks explicit tile-drain routing and lateral flow
Soil column depth and layering use ELM defaults with texture (sand/clay %) prescribed per column from representative SSURGO/USDA classes for the Upper Iowa basin
Representative flat agricultural topography assumed; free-drainage lower boundary via ELM's default groundwater scheme
Analysis quantifies texture control by comparing mean annual and seasonal QDRAI, runoff ratio, and ZWT across the five columns
